header.title: Mahabharat Episode 8: Amba’s Plight
header.description: Shantanu's sons with Satyavati, the tragic fate of Prince Chitrangada, Bhishma's abduction of the Princesses of Kashi, and Amba's heartbreaking journey of rejection.

intro.title: Shantanu's New Lineage
leads: Shantanu took his son Devavrata's life away to fulfill his own desire, just as Yayati had taken his son’s youth. With Satyavati, Shantanu fathered two sons: Chitrangada and Vichitraveerya.
In ancient times, securing a son and heir was the ultimate duty of a king, as monarchs faced daily risks of death in battle and an absent heir meant losing the entire empire.

storyElements.text: The Tragic Death of Prince Chitrangada

storyElements.html: The elder son, Chitrangada, grew into an arrogant young prince. One day while in the forest, he encountered a gandharva—a skilled celestial being—who happened to share the exact same name: Chitrangada.

bubble.text: How dare you call yourself Chitrangada? I am Chitrangada. You better change your name. This is my name. You are unfit to carry my name.
How dare you say that! It looks like you’ve lived too long. Come, let us fight because my father has named me Chitrangada and this is my name.

storyElements.html: They engaged in combat, and within moments, the young prince was killed.

storyElements.text: The Strange Prince and the Kashi Swayamvara

storyElements.html: Only one son remained: Vichitraveerya. "Vichitra" translates to strange or distorted, and "veerya" means masculinity—signifying a "distorted masculinity". He was either unwilling or incapable of securing a wife.
With Chitrangada dead, Vichitraveerya unwilling to marry, and Bhishma bound by his oath of celibacy, the future of the Kuru dynasty ground to a complete halt.

Around this time, the King of Kashi organized a Swayamvara—a royal event where eligible Kshatriya suitors gather and princesses independently select their husbands by placing a garland on their chosen groom. The King of Kashi announced the Swayamvara for his three daughters: Amba, Ambika, and Ambalika.

Despite the Kuru dynasty being the largest and most revered power in the region, the King of Kashi purposefully withheld an invitation from them, unwilling to marry his daughters to Vichitraveerya due to rumors regarding his masculinity.
Unable to tolerate this insult to the honor of the Kuru dynasty—which he prioritized above his own or anyone else's well-being—Bhishma personally rode to Kashi to attend the ceremony.
At the assembly, Princess Amba was already deeply in love with King Salva of Shalva. She walked up to Salva and placed her garland around his neck, choosing him as her husband.
Just as the choice was made, Bhishma entered the arena. Knowing he had sworn off marriage and castrated himself, the assembled warriors mocked him openly:

bubble.text: Why has the old man come here now? Is he looking for a bride? Or does the Kuru clan not have a warrior who can come and take a bride? Is that the reason he has come?

storyElements.html: Enraged by the mockery leveled against his clan and nation, Bhishma forcibly abducted all three princesses.

The rival warriors gave chase to stop him, and King Salva fought fiercely to defend his chosen bride. However, Bhishma defeated and humiliated all of them, carrying Amba, Ambika, and Ambalika away to Hastinapur.

storyElements.text: Protest on the Journey and Rejection at Court

storyElements.html: In tears during the journey, Amba confronted her captor:

bubble.text: What have you done? I was in love with this man and I had already put my garland on him. He is my husband. You can't take me like this.
I have taken you. What I take belongs to the Kurus.

storyElements.html: Upon arriving in Hastinapur, Vichitraveerya wed Ambika and Ambalika, but firmly refused to accept Amba.

bubble.text: She placed the garland on someone else. She has given her heart to someone. I will not marry this woman.
What am I supposed to do now?

storyElements.html: Realizing the predicament, Bhishma apologized to Amba and agreed to arrange for her safe return to King Salva.

bubble.text: I will arrange for you to be sent back to Salva.

storyElements.html: Relieved, Amba returned to Salva, only to face a crushing humiliation:

bubble.text: I am not here to take charity from somebody. I lost the battle. The old beast defeated me and now he is trying to give me a charity bride. I will not take you. Go back.

storyElements.html: Rejected by both suitors, Amba returned once more to Hastinapur and demanded that Bhishma take responsibility for her ruined life.

bubble.text: You’ve destroyed my life. You took away the man I love, you brought me here forcefully and the person I am supposed to marry will not marry me. You must marry me.
My allegiance is to my nation. I have given my word that I will not marry and that's all.

storyElements.html: Five thousand years ago, a princess rejected by everyone—unable to return to her father, abandoned by her true love, and refused by the royal house that abducted her—walked out alone into the wilderness in complete and absolute desolation, not knowing where she was going...
